newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Venezuela Petkoff sees Nov inflation below 3.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Petkoff sees Nov inflation below 3.6 pct.

text.p: Venezuelan Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said Thursday the monthly inflation rate for November would be below the 3.6 percent recorded in September.
He said inflation rose to 4.2 percent in October, but attributed the figure to a jump in electricity prices.
"Nevertheless, the fall in inflation seems consistent and in November it will be below the rate of September," Petkoff said in a speech in the Brazilian capital Brasilia.
Petkoff said that there were sufficient indications that the Venezuelan economy is starting to recover.

"A realistic target for next year is four percent (gross domestic product) growth for the non-petroleum economy," he said. "It will be the first, we hope the first of many years, of growth with low inflation."
Petkoff said the government had been working with a target of reducing the federal government deficit to two percent of GDP in 1996 from 8.5 percent of GDP in 1995.
"We may end the year with a small surplus," he said.
Petkoff was visiting Brazil for talks with Brazilian officials about progress on Venezuela's economic reforms, launched in April.
